author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Ben Shelton and Frances Tiafoe will meet Friday in the first Grand Slam semifinal between two Black American men in the Open Era, adding a historic milestone to the U.S. Open.

The matchup guarantees an American finalist and follows separate quarterfinal victories that moved both players within one win of the championship round. Shelton and Tiafoe have shared Arthur Ashe Stadium before: they met in the 2023 U.S. Open quarterfinals, giving Friday’s contest a recent competitive history as well as broader significance.

Tiafoe also reached the U.S. Open semifinals in 2024. Shelton has since added major hard-court credentials, including two Masters 1000 titles and a victory in Montreal in August 2026. Their progress reflects a deeper group of American men contending late at major tournaments.

The tournament also has an important parallel in the women’s draw, where Coco Gauff advanced to the semifinals after rallying past Mirra Andreeva. The Shelton-Tiafoe match should be judged on tactics and form, but its place in tennis history is already established: for the first time in the Open Era, two Black American men will share a major semifinal stage.
dek: Friday’s U.S. Open matchup will be the first Open Era Grand Slam semifinal between two Black American men, guaranteeing a home finalist.
headline: Shelton-Tiafoe semifinal makes Grand Slam history for Black American men
